note: Closes BF-2026-029. Recorded retroactively on 2026-08-08 from the run log — see provenance below.

provenance.capture_method: extracted from the GitHub Actions run log after the fact
provenance.why_retroactive: The teardown was dispatched to stop an active $14.40/day burn before any AWS read access existed in the session. No live pre-teardown probe was taken.
provenance.why_no_live_probe_was_possible: The Kubernetes chart was never installed into the cluster (no helm install or kubectl apply exists in .github/ or scripts/; scripts/kubernetes/reset-scenario.mjs states live apply is out of scope). The cluster served no public endpoint, and its API server requires authentication, so there was nothing equivalent to an HTTP smoke capture.
provenance.strength: Terraform's own destroy record with real AWS resource identifiers is the authoritative account of what existed. It is stronger than a screenshot for provenance and weaker only in that it shows resources being removed rather than serving traffic.
provenance.retention_risk: GitHub Actions logs expire (~90 days). This file exists so the record survives that expiry.

retained_deliberately.reason: Cents per month; keeps the lab re-appliable on demand.

cost_evidence.rate_explanation: Kubernetes 1.32 left EKS standard support on 2026-03-23, so the control plane billed extended support at $0.60/hr rather than $0.10 — 6x the repository's own cost model.
cost_evidence.uptime_source: Creation stamp embedded in the destroyed IAM role name cops-staging-eks-cluster-20260718131629731200000007

verified_stop.method: Cost Explorer daily granularity by service
verified_stop.interpretation: $0.582 / $0.60 = 0.97 hours, consistent with the 01:00:47Z teardown to within four minutes.

claim_impact: None. README records hosted evidence as tip-inherited from recorded runs rather than re-applied on every tip, so no claim in docs/claims/matrix.json depended on the cluster remaining live.
